# Format:   STATE | group | agent | task | seed | extra flags
#   STATE:  ON | OFF (skip) | RUNNING (in flight) | DONE
#   horizon_length = 1 (no action chunking),  best_of_n = 1,  no base_scale
#   eval episodes: 50 by default, 100 for phase-3 rows (EVAL_EPISODES env)
#   R07 action + data-anchor + kl  = 0.524   <-- beats rebrac
#   R05 absolute + data + no-reg   = 0.456   <-- beats rebrac
DONE | R03_pre_res_kl_t3  | agents/anq_rfs.py   | 3 | 0 |   # 0.028  residual anchor fails

# PHASE 3: validate the winner.  3 tasks x 3 seeds, eval_episodes=100.
# Matching rebrac baselines at the same seeds so the comparison is paired.
# runner-up (R05) on all three tasks, seed 0 only, as a cheap cross-check
# PHASE 3b: EXTRA SEEDS for statistical power.  Run-to-run std on t3 is ~0.12
# and the effect size is ~0.10, so n=3 cannot resolve it (delta = +0.085 +- 0.104).
# These take t3 to n=8 and t1 to n=6 per arm.  Inserted AHEAD of the ablations.
# PHASE 4: tasks 4 and 5 (never run before -- no archive baseline exists).
# Paired anq_rfs vs rebrac, 3 seeds each, eval_episodes=100.
# PHASE 2b: ablations, re-pointed onto the winning "action" composition
# (was pretanh; pretanh placed 7th/8th so it is not worth more GPU time).
# bc_anchor=residual is dropped entirely - it scored 0.028 / 0.004.
# ---- SAC-style variants, on the winning "action" composition --------------
# PHASE 5: target_multiplier sweep (latent KL budget = target_multiplier * 8).
# It sat at the inherited anq_stdfp default 0.125 and was never tuned; the only
# alternative tried was 0.5 (R15b) which scored 0.292 vs 0.478 on t3 seed 0.
# Baseline for comparison: winner at 0.125 already has n=8 on t3 (0.378).
# 3 seeds per value.  Also seeding R17b (live base), flagged earlier as the
# best single ablation (0.496 at n=1) but never replicated.
# PHASE 6: seed the two best single-seed arms.
#   SE = S01b: SAC entropy on the LATENT only, deterministic residual.
#        Scored 0.516 at n=1 -- the highest t3 result in the project.
#        (entropy + STOCHASTIC residual collapsed to 0.000 at every scale.)
#   Also entropy_scale sweep around it, since it was never tuned either.
# Every arm so far samples z in the actor loss (train_latent_stochastic=True),
# including latent_reg=none.  This sets train_latent_stochastic=False so z is
# the mean, std receives no gradient at all, and there is no latent penalty:
# a purely deterministic latent head, DDPG-style.
# DET  = deterministic latent, no regulariser  (the clean DDPG ablation)
# DETK = deterministic latent, KL kept         (isolates sampling from the KL)
# PHASE 8: sigreg -- the DDPG-compatible latent regulariser from stdfp.py.
# A deterministic latent head has no per-sample distribution, so KL/entropy
# degenerate.  sigreg instead matches the BATCH MARGINAL of z to N(0,I) by
# empirical-characteristic-function regression, which is well defined for a
# deterministic head.  Sanity-checked: 1.22 on true N(0,I), 245.8 when shifted.
# SIG  = deterministic latent + sigreg   (the pairing this is designed for)
# SIGS = stochastic latent + sigreg      (does it help even when sampling?)
# coeff sweep on the deterministic variant since sigreg_coeff is untuned (1.0).
# PHASE 9: cube-double manipulation (CD_ prefix -> h=5, chunking on, disc 0.99).
# DSRL reports strong results here with a TanhNormal latent at
# target_multiplier=0.5.  anq_rfs uses an UNSQUASHED latent, so this tests
# whether that choice costs us on manipulation.
# NOTE full_action_dim = 5 act-dim x 5 horizon = 25, so a tanh latent carries
# an irreducible KL floor of ~11.4 nats (measured at init); target_kl=12.5
# leaves only ~1.1 nats of usable budget.
# DSRL's own default is regularizer=entropy w/ target_entropy_multiplier=0.5,
# so both readings of 'target_multiplier=0.5' are run.
# lam=0.01 on cube-double was an UNTUNED carry-over from antmaze.  The penalty
# is lam * sum_dims (a-a_data)^2 with 25 dims here vs 8 on antmaze, and the
# measured equilibrium bc_offset is 2.85 (cube) vs 0.36 (antmaze) -- i.e. the
# anchor is not holding and the policy leaves the manifold the decoder learned
# (which fits fine here: generated_to_data_mse 0.018 vs 0.071 on antmaze).
# latent_only removes the residual entirely so the action can ONLY come from
# the decoder -- the DSRL structure, which reaches 0.81 here.
# Q term is norm_q-scaled to O(1); bc_offset equilibrates at 2.85, so lam must
# reach ~0.35 merely to be comparable, and the fixed point moves as lam rises.
# lam=100 is effectively pure BC of the dataset action -- a useful reference
# PHASE 11: cube-double with SHARP drift BC (drift_temps 0.1-0.25) x moderate lam.
# drift_temps=3.0 was, like lam=0.01, an antmaze carry-over.  R is the kernel
# radius in drift_loss: large R -> near-uniform affinities -> weak, blurred
# forces.  stdfp.py scores well on this domain and its config default is 0.1.
# PHASE 12: latent_only x SHARP drift BC -- the two changes that each helped,
# never yet combined.  latent_only alone: 0.115 (peaks 0.36 @100-200k then
# decays 65%).  drift_temps=0.1 gives a 6x looser decoder fit (mse 0.117 vs
# 0.0195), which is the diversity the decayed runs were losing.
# PHASE 13: match stdfp.py's actor objective (no structural change to anq_rfs).
# stdfp's actor loss is (alpha*KL - Q) with NO anchor on the executed action;
# behaviour is constrained only by the BC'd decoder + the latent KL.  My earlier
# latent_only runs still carried lam*||base - a_data||^2 (bc_anchor=data), which
# back-props through the decoder into z and fights the Q steering.  bc_anchor
# =none removes it.  stdfp also defaults to target_multiplier=0.5, not 0.125.
# NOTE this also re-tests drift_temps: the earlier 0.1-vs-3.0 comparison was
# confounded by that anchor term, so 0.1 has not had a fair test.
# PHASE 14: q_agg=mean on cube.  q_agg gates the TD target (line 291,
# next_q = aggregate(next_qs)); 'min' over the 2-critic ensemble is a pessimism
# knob inherited from antmaze and can be far too conservative on manipulation.
# Paired against the CDN* arms which are identical except q_agg=min.

# PHASE 17: DSRL behavioural diff, one factor at a time (best_of_n=1, num_qs=2
# pinned).  Base = current best cube config.  The three non-structural deltas:
#   samp: dsrl samples the latent at execution AND in the TD target
#   tgt:  dsrl decodes through the EMA'd flow (use_target_latent) -- a
#         stationary latent space; ours chased a live decoder (likely the
#   pess: dsrl's backup is mean - 0.5*std, NOT min.  (my earlier 'mean fails'

# PHASE 18 (user direction): stdfp.py IS the working base on manipulation; its
# disease is drift-BC overfitting.  anq_stdfp = stdfp + refine actor, and with
# high lam on the RESIDUAL anchor (refine_anchor=base -> ||delta||^2) it should
# recover stdfp.  Fix = bc_stop_step: decoder is trained only by drift BC, so
# zeroing that loss after N steps freezes it before it overfits (verified:
# decoder grad exactly 0 past the stop; Adam momentum dies in ~200 steps).
# stdfp defaults kept: sac latent, kl reg, tm=0.5, drift_temps=0.1, num_qs=2,
# best_of_n=1.  CDF_* -> cube-double h=5 disc 0.99 via the CD* domain case.
# ---- phase 18b: 3rd seeds for the winners + earlier stop -------------------
# sfstop3 works (0.40-0.47), sfstop6 too late; bracket from the other side.
# ---- phase 18c: stop-time is monotone toward earlier (200k>300k>>600k>never)
# push the bracket down and give the refine version the better stop point.
# stop-time still improving at 150k/100k; bracket 50k.  refine version gets the
# best stop (150k) and a lam=30 variant to shrink its 0.12 gap vs matched stdfp.
# ---- lam=100 rung: lam=30 (0.542) > lam=10 (0.483) at matched stop, so the
# 'sufficiently high lam' trend is confirmed and one more rung should converge
# Larger eps damps per-param normalisation where the 2nd moment is tiny (the
# latent actor once Q stabilises).  Tested on the two best configs.
# ---- eps as ALTERNATIVE to bc_stop (user clarification): stock stdfp, no stop.
# Hypothesis: large eps damps the drift-BC updates once its gradients shrink,
# preventing the late overfitting without a hard cutoff.
# ---- eps=1e-3 BREAKTHROUGH: stock stdfp 0.740/0.740, no decay, evals to 0.86.
# Extend: 3rd seed, eps=3e-3 probe, and eps=1e-3 on the refine version (no stop).
# ---- phase 18f: drift-loss normalization is the ROOT CAUSE (user's pointer).
# Measured: actor_drift_loss = 1.000 at every step of every run -- the unit-RMS
# force normalization makes the BC gradient invariant to fit quality, so the
# decoder chases re-inflated noise forever.  eps=1e-3 was the optimizer-side
# damp; force_norm=raw is the loss-level fix (BC push anneals with actual force).
# Test raw at DEFAULT eps (1e-8): if it alone prevents the collapse, mechanism
# ---- phase 18g: finish line.  eps=3e-3 > 1e-3 for stdfp (0.804 vs 0.680);
# give the refine version the same eps, add eps=1e-2 bracket + 3rd seeds.
# ---- phase 18h: DECODER-ONLY eps (removes the global-eps damping trade-off).
# drift_adam_eps applies the large eps to actor_drift only; critic and latent
# actor keep 1e-8.  If the mechanism story is right this should match or beat
# ---- phase 18i: options 2 & 3, each at DEFAULT eps to isolate the mechanism.
# (option 4, validation-based stop, dropped per user: it leaks held-out
#  supervision into a training decision -- cheating vs baselines.)
# opt2: linear BC-weight decay 100k->400k (smooth version of bc_stop).
# opt3: force_norm=const 0.055 (early-training force RMS): full-strength BC at
#       the start, anneals as the true force decays relative to the constant.
# ---- user suggestion: raw force + DECODER-ONLY eps=1e-4 --------------------
# raw alone: decoder grads ~30x small -> underfit/decay (0.36).  raw + GLOBAL
# eps=1e-3: dead (~0.0, everything damped).  raw + drift_adam_eps=1e-4 keeps
# early decoder updates at lr scale (sqrt(v) > eps) and anneals once the true
# force decays below the floor -- raw's annealing with unit-norm's early speed.
# Evidence it is reachable: sfe33 s0 ENDED at 0.94; several curves still rising
# at the 1M cutoff now that the eps fix cures the decay.
# A: anq_rfs finally gets the winning recipe (residual anchor, lam=10, tm=0.5,
#    drift_temps=0.1, q_agg=min) + eps -- it never had these fixes.
# B: 3M-step runs (CDX_ prefix) of the two best known configs.
# C: eps fine grid around the 3e-3 optimum.

# ---- q_agg=mean (user direction).  NOTE the earlier 'mean gives 0.000' was

# ---- 3rd seeds for the two leaders (sfe33m 0.828, tm0125 0.786) ------------

# 2) lam bracket on the rfs leader: lam=10 was carried from anq_stdfp, never
#    swept under the current cube recipe
# 3) anq_stdfp + q_agg=mean: its 0.744 used min; mean was worth +0.06 on stdfp

# unregularised.  If lam=10 works on antmaze too, the domain story collapses to
# 'drift anchor fine everywhere at proper lam; DATA anchor is the domain knob'.
# PHASE 20: >=0.9 with anq_rfs.  Key find: stdfp (0.845) EXECUTES STOCHASTICALLY
# (dist.sample at eval + stochastic TD target); every rfs arm so far used the
# mode.  P1/P2 = stdfp's exact winning form inside anq_rfs: latent_only (residual

# ---- wake 6: lam=1 DETERMINISTIC beat the lam=10 leader at n=1 (0.792 vs

# ---- wake 7: lam=0.3 hit 0.840 n=1 with an ACTIVE residual (drms 0.0099).
# Seed it on t2; carry lam-freedom to every gap task; stdfp-family diagnostic
